passages.notes: Tests throne/pasture/fang/fleece and the criterion of the Good Shepherd.
Tests authority and Unclaimed Virtue through Christ's refusal to exploit status.
Strong control for authority-as-service.
Embodied authority without possession.
Important for 'remaining' and Christological dependence.
Tests love/fear and divine priority.
Supports fruit test without self-certification.

Tests concrete mercy and Christological judgment. Preserve the dispute over whether 'the least of these my brothers' refers especially to disciples/emissaries, people in need generally, or a broader group.
Threshold/crossing resonance; avoid flattening historical context.
Important for non-retaliatory fidelity and communal gifts.
Useful but must not be made to erase concrete difference.
Important for subordination/reconciliation of powers.
Useful for obedience/mercy over self-display.
Tests liturgical truth through embodied justice.
Major OT shepherd-control passage.
Primary control against making Troth an autonomous preexistent principle or second Logos.
Controls the Shepherd/Lamb paradox while reserving Christ's saving self-gift and worship from ordinary lamb figures.
Controls morning: transformation preserves identity and bodily history without authorizing a mythic claim of literal universal resurrection.
Supports accountability without self-certification. Universal sin must not be used to claim equal culpability in every concrete conflict.
Joins concrete responsibility to a genuine possibility of turning and rejects guilt as inherited immutable identity.
Joins divine initiative and joy to human response and concrete repair without reducing all return stories to one mechanism.
Distinguishes productive repentance from emotional distress. Its disputed historical situation prevents use as a universal checklist or demand for visible sorrow.
Controls communal correction and return. Preserve the Matthew 18:15 textual variant and do not collapse forgiveness, reconciliation, safety, trust, or office restoration.
Firmly controls vengeance and enemy-love. Preserve rival readings of the concrete sayings as active nonviolent resistance, radical nonresistance, rhetorical intensification, or personal ethics.
Preserves canonical tension: authority has real responsibility, but office and power do not certify righteousness or command unlimited obedience.
Historically addresses enslaved household members. Never use it to require an abused person to remain accessible to harm, preserve an institution, or treat suffering as salvific currency.
Supports differentiated callings without a ladder of holiness and joins greater responsibility to greater accountability.
Offers a pattern of accountable deliberation but not an infallible constitution; preserve historical questions about its relation to Galatians 2.
Hearing the cry issues in attention and action. Use Deuteronomy 19:15-21 and Proverbs 18:13, 17 as controls for corroboration and inquiry.
Controls the Black Sun by distinguishing testimony and the Lamb's victory from the accuser's totalizing verdict.
